PLAINTIFE’S MOTION TO DISQUALIFY MAGISTRATE JUDGE IVAN D. DAVIS
UNDER 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4) AND § 455(a), AND FOR PRIORITY DETERMINATION

Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine, proceeding pro se, moves under 28 U.S.C. § 455 for the
disqualification of Magistrate Judge Ivan D. Davis from further participation in this action and for
priority determination of this Motion. The grounds are stated below and in the accompanying
Memorandum in Support. Exhibit A, Exhibit B, and the Declaration of Marvelle J. Ballentine
accompany this Motion.

I. STATUTORY BASIS AND RELIEF
This Motion rests on 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4). That subsection requires a magistrate judge to

disqualify himself when he knows that he has a financial interest in a party to the proceeding. The
Motion rests independently on 28 U.S.C. § 455(a), which requires disqualification in any

proceeding in which the judge’s impartiality might reasonably be questioned. Sections 455(c),

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 86 Filed 10/13/26 Page 2 of 9 PagelD# 824

455(d)(4), 455(e), and 455(f) govern the duty to inform, the definition of financial interest,
nonwaiver, and the divestiture exception.

The Motion presents one question of fact and one question of law. The question of fact is
whether a financial interest in Defendant Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta’’) was held during Magistrate
Judge Davis’s participation in this action. The question of law is whether, on the facts determined,
§ 455 requires disqualification.

The Motion alleges no bias, hostility, improper motive, bad faith, or intentional
nondisclosure. It rests on two signed financial disclosure reports and the docket.

II. FINANCIAL-DISCLOSURE FACTS
Exhibit A is Magistrate Judge Davis’s Financial Disclosure Report (AO Form 10) for

calendar year 2025. Judge Davis electronically signed it on May 14, 2026 and on May 26, 2026.
Ex. A at 1. Part VII, line 6, identifies “FB common stock” with a gross year-end value of $15,001—
$50,000 and dividend income of $1,000 or less. Ex. A at 2. No transaction is reported on that line.
The same report records purchases and sales of other securities during 2025. Ex. A at 3 (Part VU,
lines 37-40).

Exhibit B is Magistrate Judge Davis’s Financial Disclosure Report for calendar year 2024,
dated August 18, 2025. Part VII, line 6, identifies “FB common stock” with value code K
($15,001-$50,000) and income code A ($1,000 or less). Ex. B at 4. No transaction is reported on
that line.

Both reports identify common-stock holdings by trading symbol. Ex. A at 2—3 (Part VII,
lines 4-6, 16-34); Ex. B at 4-6 (Part VII, lines 4-6, 16-18, 20-35). “FB” was the Nasdaq trading
symbol for the Class A common stock of Facebook, Inc. Facebook, Inc. changed its corporate

name to Meta Platforms, Inc. on October 28, 2021. The trading symbol for the same stock changed

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 86 Filed 10/13/26 Page 3 of 9 PagelD# 825

to “META” in June 2022. The Memorandum in Support, Part II.B, identifies the public filings with
the Securities and Exchange Commission that establish those facts.

The reports establish that Judge Davis reported holding “FB common stock” at the close of
2024 and at the close of 2025. Whether that holding continued through the period of Judge Davis’s
participation in this action is an inference from the reports. It is not an established fact. This Motion
asks the Court to determine it.

II. PARTICIPATION IN THE ACTION
Plaintiff filed this action on July 30, 2026, naming Meta as a defendant. ECF No. 1. The

First Amended Complaint names Meta. ECF No. 5. Meta appeared through counsel, moved to
dismiss, and filed its corporate disclosure statement on August 21, 2026. ECF Nos. 21, 22, 24.

The Clerk’s docket assigns Magistrate Judge Davis to this action. On August 25, 2026, the
Clerk set Plaintiff’s motions at ECF Nos. 15 and 26 for hearing before Judge Davis on September
25, 2026. On September 8, 2026, the Clerk set ECF No. 54 for hearing before Judge Davis on the
same date.

Judge Davis entered six orders. ECF No. 62 (Sept. 9, 2026) treated ECF No. 26 as
withdrawn. ECF No. 63 (Sept. 9, 2026) denied ECF No. 41 as moot, terminated the hearing on ECF
No. 15, and required any party using generative artificial intelligence to identify that use and certify
citation review. ECF No. 64 (Sept. 9, 2026) required Plaintiff to file, by September 11, 2026, a
redlined version of the proposed amended complaint showing changes against the original
Complaint, ECF No. 1. ECF No. 65 (Sept. 10, 2026) terminated the hearing on ECF No. 54, set
Meta’s response and Plaintiff’s reply dates, and restated the certification requirement. ECF No. 82
(Sept. 22, 2026) granted ECF No. 78 and restated the certification requirement. ECF No. 84 (Oct.

7, 2026) is described next.

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 86 Filed 10/13/26 Page 4 of 9 PagelD# 826

ECF No. 84 denied as premature Plaintiff's motions for leave to serve limited
interrogatories on NCMEC (ECF No. 15) and on Meta (ECF No. 54). ECF No. 84 describes those
motions as “requests for expedited discovery concerning Defendants National Center for Missing
& Exploited Children ((“NCMEC’) and Meta Platforms, Inc., respectively.” ECF No. 84 at 1. ECF
No. 84 also denied Plaintiff’s motion for leave to file a Second Amended and Supplemental
Complaint (ECF No. 59), stating that Plaintiff “has failed” to produce the redline required by ECF
No. 64. ECF No. 84 at 2.

Every order listed above was entered after Meta became a party. ECF No. 84 expressly
addresses discovery directed to Meta.

IV. TIMELINESS

Plaintiff was unaware of the reported financial interest when ECF No. 84 was entered on
October 7, 2026, and at every earlier point in this action, and promptly presented this Motion after
learning of it through the Financial Disclosure Reports database maintained by the Administrative
Office of the United States Courts. Ballentine Decl. §] 2—3. Kolon Indus. Inc. v. E.I. du Pont de
Nemours & Co., 748 F.3d 160, 169-71 (4th Cir. 2014), applies the prompt-presentation
requirement to motions under § 455(b); the judge’s independent obligation under § 455 does not
eliminate that requirement.

V. REQUESTED DETERMINATION

Plaintiff requests that the Court state on the record: (a) whether the asset reported as “FB
common stock” on Exhibits A and B is common stock of Meta Platforms, Inc.; (b) whether that
interest was held on July 30, 2026, and on each date on which ECF Nos. 62, 63, 64, 65, 82, and 84
were entered; (c) the date and manner of any divestiture; (d) whether the interest is held directly or
through a mutual or common investment fund within the meaning of 28 U.S.C. § 455(d)(4)(i); and

(e) any other fact the Court considers material to the application of 28 U.S.C. § 455(f).

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 86 Filed 10/13/26 Page 5 of 9 PagelD# 827

Upon determination of those facts, Plaintiff requests a determination whether 28 U.S.C. §
455(b)(4) or § 455(a) requires disqualification. If disqualification is required, Plaintiff requests an
order of disqualification and the ministerial steps necessary to return or transfer the referred matters
through the Court’s assignment procedures.

VI. RELATED PROCEEDINGS
Plaintiff’s Rule 72(a) objections to ECF Nos. 63, 64, and 65 (ECF No. 66), Plaintiff’s

motion to set aside ECF No. 64 (ECF No. 67), and Plaintiff’s motion for leave to file a notice of
subsequent record development (ECF No. 76) are pending before District Judge Alston. On
October 12, 2026, Plaintiff submitted through the Court’s Electronic Document Submission
System a Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument as to ECF Nos. 66, 67, and 76, requesting
determination of those motions on the papers under Local Civil Rule 7(J).

Concurrently with this Motion, Plaintiff submits Rule 72(a) objections to ECF No. 84 anda
separate application to District Judge Alston to withdraw or modify the referral and for targeted
vacatur of ECF Nos. 64 and 84. Those filings seek the retrospective and case-management
remedies. This Motion does not. This Motion asks Judge Davis to determine the statutory
disqualification question and the facts on which it depends. Neither this Motion nor the companion
filings extends the time to object under Rule 72(a) or replaces any pending objection.

Plaintiff reserves review under Rule 72(a) of any order disposing of this Motion.

VII. CONCLUSION AND RELIEF REQUESTED

Plaintiff requests that the Court:
Al.  Disqualify Magistrate Judge Davis under 28 U.S.C. § 455(b)(4), and alternatively

under 28 U.S.C. § 455(a), upon determination of the facts identified in Part V;

Case 1:26-cv-02331-RDA-IDD Document 86 Filed 10/13/26 Page 6 of 9 PagelD# 828

A2. — State on the record whether the reported interest was held during the challenged
participation, the date and manner of any divestiture, and the facts necessary to determine any
claimed exception under 28 U.S.C. § 455(f);

A3. Determine this Motion before taking any further substantive action in this matter;

A4. — Upon disqualification, return or transfer the referred matters through the Court’s
assignment procedures; and

A5. Determine this Motion on the papers, in a written disposition sufficient to identify
the grounds of decision.

Plaintiff waives oral argument and requests determination on the papers under Local Civil
Rule 7(J) and Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 78(b). A Notice of Waiver of Oral Argument under

Local Civil Rule 7(E) accompanies this Motion. A proposed order accompanies this Motion.
